findings: https://shop.doublebasshq.com/products/bad-brothers — Samples explicitly label Double Bass 1–4. grade.basis: Representative publisher score pages 1, 3 and 5: upper-register bass playing and harmonic accuracy, contrasting bow/pizzicato roles, chromatic syncopation and improvisation require pre-diploma command across the group. Moderate swing and repeated patterns constrain the difficulty; no virtuoso improvisation is assumed. Ensemble precision is included within level 6, with no additional uplift.

Idiomatic repeated material makes this advanced rather than diploma repertoire. The steadiness and ensemble articulation fit within level 5; no extra uplift.

grade.basis: No musical notation available in supplied evidence. Big-band style, performer reputation and descriptive claims cannot establish register, technical demands or a defensible whole-work level. Hold level and hardest-part approval until notation is available.

findings: https://shop.doublebasshq.com/products/compostela — Publisher opening score and first-bass page show Allegro quarter=120, sustained accented upper-register sixteenths, ricochet responses in basses 2–3, and subsequent slurred figures/double stops in bass 1. Included Bass World review specifies thumb-position fluency and a recurring G-minor theme.

grade.basis: The exposed upper-register repeated sixteenths require bow stamina and control, followed by slurred register movement and double stops; thumb-position fluency is corroborated by the publisher-hosted review. Repeated ostinati and the fourth-bass rhythmic foundation moderate the coordination burden. Pre-diploma level 6 fits the sustained technical demand; no separate uplift beyond it.

findings: https://shop.doublebasshq.com/products/the-river-fisherman — Publisher score excerpts show four bass staves, medium swing, chromatic articulated lines, arco/pizzicato changes, rests and offbeat attacks, and a later treble-register passage shared by basses 1–3. Publisher describes an intermediate quartet.

grade.basis: Representative publisher score excerpts include the opening, bars 11–19 and bars 39 onward. Bass 1 carries exposed high-register chromatic eighth-note phrases while basses 2–3 also enter treble register; the group must coordinate short syncopated attacks and bow/pizzicato transitions. The upper-register intonation and shifting place the hardest part around pre-diploma, moderated by medium swing and recurring material. Level 6 includes ensemble demands without an added uplift; no unseen virtuoso passages are assumed.
